profiles.note: An approved customer-owned modem removes the provider gateway entirely. When the Xfinity gateway stays in place, Xfinity documents a bridge-mode procedure for using a customer-owned router with it.
An authorized customer-owned modem hands off Ethernet to a customer router, which keeps routing in one place. Bridge behaviour of a rented Spectrum gateway is not covered by a reviewed source here.
A certified customer-owned modem hands off Ethernet to a customer router. Bridge behaviour of a rented Panoramic gateway is not covered by a reviewed source here.
The AT&T gateway stays in the path. AT&T documents a passthrough/DMZ+ arrangement that hands the public address to one downstream device instead of a true bridge.

The ONT terminates fiber and can hand off Ethernet directly to a customer router, so no second routing layer is required for internet service. Verizon TV and in-home app features may depend on Verizon equipment.
The T-Mobile gateway must remain the routing device. It does not offer bridge mode, so a customer-owned router or mesh belongs downstream in access-point mode to avoid a second routing layer.
